part.name: Saddle_Block_With_Bottom_Window
part.description: Rectangular prismatic block (BBox 2 x 6 x 1.5) with a concave cylindrical saddle on the top side and a large rectangular window/pocket opened from the bottom. The bottom window has vertical walls (x=±0.8, y=±2.8) and a mixed ceiling made of a central concave cylindrical patch plus small flat end pads. Identified functional/structural features: top cylindrical cradle interface; top end flats (bearing/stop pads); bottom window/pocket (clearance/lightweighting); pocket ceiling (inner curved relief) and pocket end ceiling flats; outer perimeter structural walls; sharp/implicit edge breaks between pads/saddle and window frame.
part.symmetry_note: Geometry is symmetric about the X=0 plane and Y=0 plane (mirrored left/right and end-to-end).

Section.name: Outer Structural Shell
features included: Bottom outer frame face (annular face around window opening)
Section.function intent: Provide overall stiffness, define the outer envelope, and provide the primary load path between the top saddle interface and any external mounting/abutment surfaces.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a short beam/block: carries compressive/bending loads from the top cradle into the full-width end blocks and side walls; the bottom frame around the window behaves as a ring/edge stiffener resisting local bending around the pocket opening.
Section.geometry: Prismatic outer block with full-width side faces at x=±1 and end faces at y=±3. Bottom face is a planar frame (outer rectangle with an inner rectangular cutout).
Section.location: Entire exterior boundary of the part (all outer faces except the top saddle surfaces).

major_faces.name: Bottom outer frame
major_faces.description: Planar face at z=-0.75 with an inner rectangular opening (frame/ring around the bottom window).

major_faces.name: End face (-Y)
major_faces.description: Outer planar end face at y=-3 (full width and height).

major_faces.name: Outer side face (+X)
major_faces.description: Outer planar side face at x=+1 (full length in y and full height in z).

major_faces.description: Outer planar end face at y=+3 (full width and height).

major_faces.name: Outer side face (-X)
major_faces.description: Outer planar side face at x=-1 (full length in y and full height in z).

Section.name: Top Saddle / Contact Interface
Section.function intent: Locate and support a mating cylindrical/rounded component (or distribute contact pressure) while providing defined end pads that can act as stops or bearing lands.
Section.physical behavior: The concave cylindrical patch spreads contact load over a curved area (reducing peak stress) and tends to self-center a mating round component laterally. End flats provide local planar support and limit rocking/overtravel at the ends.
Section.geometry: One concave cylindrical surface spanning the central length region, with two planar top pads at the ends (z=+0.75) transitioning to the outer end faces.
Section.location: Top side of the part (z near +0.75), central region plus two end pads.

major_faces.name: Top end pad (-Y)
major_faces.description: Planar top surface patch at z=+0.75 near the -Y end (y from -3 to about -2.4).

major_faces.name: Top saddle cylinder
major_faces.description: Concave cylindrical surface forming the main saddle (cylinder radius 4.215, axis along X).

major_faces.name: Top end pad (+Y)
major_faces.description: Planar top surface patch at z=+0.75 near the +Y end (y from about +2.4 to +3).

Section.name: Bottom Window / Pocket (Clearance & Lightweighting)
features included: Pocket ceiling (inner relief): central concave cylinder + end flats
Section.function intent: Provide clearance for an underlying component or fastener envelope and reduce mass while preserving a perimeter frame for stiffness.
Section.physical behavior: Removes low-stress interior material to reduce weight; remaining vertical walls and ceiling act as local stiffeners defining the cavity boundaries. The concave ceiling can improve clearance to round components and reduce stress concentration compared to a sharp internal corner.
Section.geometry: Rectangular opening from the bottom with four vertical planar walls. The pocket ceiling is a central concave cylindrical patch (larger radius than the top saddle) blended by two small planar ceiling pads at the ends (z=+0.55).
Section.location: Bottom side interior, centered about the part origin; opening spans roughly x=±0.8 and y=±2.8, rising upward to the ceiling surfaces.
